cards.front: Which service finds objects, scenes, faces, celebrities and text in images and videos?
cards.back: **Amazon Rekognition** (computer vision as an API).

cards.front: In Rekognition content moderation, what does the MinConfidence parameter do, and what is its default?
cards.back: Labels detected with lower confidence are **not returned**. Default is **50**. Higher threshold = fewer false positives but more misses.

cards.front: How do you send borderline Rekognition moderation results to human reviewers?
cards.back: Create a human review workflow in **Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)** and pass it in `HumanLoopConfig` on `DetectModerationLabels`; matching images go to a private workforce, vendors or Mechanical Turk.
cards.updated: A2I entered maintenance: not available to new customers from 30 July 2026

cards.front: Rekognition face search vs face detection: what is the difference?
cards.back: **Detection/analysis** finds faces and attributes (age range, emotions, glasses). **Search** compares a face against faces you indexed in a **face collection** to identify or verify a person.

cards.front: Which Rekognition video feature from the course has been discontinued?
cards.back: **People pathing** (tracking people's paths through a video), end of support **31 October 2025**.

cards.front: Which service converts speech to text, and what technology does it use?
cards.back: **Amazon Transcribe**, using automatic speech recognition (**ASR**). Batch jobs on files in S3 or real-time streaming.

cards.front: Call recordings must be transcribed without customers' card numbers and names. Which feature?
cards.back: **Transcribe PII redaction**: identified PII is replaced by `[PII]` in the transcript (optionally keep an unredacted copy too).

cards.front: Audio contains several languages and you do not know which. Which Transcribe feature helps?
cards.back: **Automatic language identification** (single dominant language or multi-language identification). Note: batch PII redaction cannot be combined with it.

cards.front: Which service turns text into lifelike speech?
cards.back: **Amazon Polly** (engines: standard, neural, long-form, generative).

cards.front: Polly: how do you make a brand name or acronym always be pronounced a specific way?
cards.back: Upload a **pronunciation lexicon** (W3C PLS XML with alias or phoneme) and reference it in `SynthesizeSpeech`; up to **5 lexicons** per request.

cards.front: Polly: what is SSML used for? Give three examples.
cards.back: Markup that controls delivery per request: pauses (`<break>`), emphasis, phonetic pronunciation, **whispering**, breathing, **newscaster** style, substitutions.

cards.front: Which Polly engine is needed for whispering and emphasis, and which for the newscaster style?
cards.back: Whispering, breathing and emphasis: **standard** voices only. Newscaster: **neural** engine with select voices (Matthew, Joanna, Amy, Lupe).
cards.updated: Tag support now differs across four engines

cards.front: Which service localizes website content into other languages?
cards.back: **Amazon Translate** (neural machine translation, 75 languages, real-time or batch; custom terminology for brand names).

cards.front: When Translate's source language is set to auto, which service detects the language?
cards.back: **Amazon Comprehend**, called by Translate on your behalf (may add a Comprehend charge).

cards.front: Name five insights Amazon Comprehend extracts from text.
cards.back: Dominant **language**, **entities**, **key phrases**, **sentiment** (positive/negative/neutral/mixed), targeted sentiment, **syntax**, **PII**.

cards.front: What happened to Comprehend topic modeling?
cards.back: Since **30 April 2026** topic modeling (plus event detection and prompt safety) is **not available to new customers**; recent users keep access. AWS suggests Bedrock models instead.

cards.front: Which service extracts conditions, medications and PHI from doctors' notes?
cards.back: **Amazon Comprehend Medical**; `DetectPHI` finds protected health information. HIPAA eligible, US English text.

cards.front: Amazon Lex: which two technologies does it combine?
cards.back: **Automatic speech recognition** (speech to text) and **natural language understanding** (intent recognition). Same technology as Alexa.

cards.front: In a Lex bot, what are intents, slots and fulfillment?
cards.back: **Intent** = what the user wants; **slots** = data the intent needs (date, time); **fulfillment** = usually a **Lambda** function that completes the action.

cards.front: What is Amazon Connect, and what is it called now?
cards.back: A cloud-based virtual **contact center** (phone numbers, flows, queues, agents, CRM integration), pay per use. Renamed **Amazon Connect Customer** in 2026.

cards.front: Which service extracts forms (key-value pairs) and tables from scanned documents?
cards.back: **Amazon Textract** (`AnalyzeDocument` with FORMS, TABLES, QUERIES; `AnalyzeExpense` for invoices; `AnalyzeID` for IDs).

cards.front: Textract limits: sync vs async processing?
cards.back: **Sync**: one page, up to 10 MB. **Async** (S3): multi-page PDF/TIFF up to **500 MB** and **3,000 pages**. Handwriting: English only.

cards.front: Which service answers natural-language questions over internal documents, and what is its status?
cards.back: **Amazon Kendra** (ML-powered enterprise search, incremental learning). In maintenance since 30 June 2026 and **closed to new customers from 30 July 2026**; AWS recommends Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

cards.front: Which service gives real-time product recommendations and re-ranking without building ML models?
cards.back: **Amazon Personalize** (data from S3 plus real-time events; outputs to websites, apps, email, SMS).

cards.front: When should you choose SageMaker AI over a managed AI service?
cards.back: When you need a **custom model** trained on your own data for a problem no AI service covers, and you have ML skills. Otherwise a managed AI service has less operational overhead.

cards.front: SageMaker AI inference: which option for large payloads (up to 1 GB) or processing up to one hour?
cards.back: **Asynchronous inference** (requests are queued). Real-time endpoints = low latency; serverless = spiky traffic; batch transform = offline scoring of a data set.

cards.front: Polly: SynthesizeSpeech vs StartSpeechSynthesisTask?
cards.back: **SynthesizeSpeech** streams audio back in near real time, up to **3,000** billed characters. **StartSpeechSynthesisTask** is asynchronous: up to **100,000** billed characters, output written to an **S3** bucket, optional **SNS** notification.

cards.front: Scanned images of doctors' notes must be checked for PHI. Which services, in which order?
cards.back: **Textract** first (turn the image into text), then **Comprehend Medical `DetectPHI`**. Comprehend Medical only reads text.

cards.front: Which machine learning services are on the current SAA-C03 in-scope list?
cards.back: Eight: **Comprehend, Lex, Polly, Rekognition, SageMaker AI, Textract, Transcribe, Translate**. Kendra, Personalize and Connect are taught in the course but not listed (the list is non-exhaustive).
cards.updated: Current in-scope list names SageMaker AI

cards.front: Which Rekognition features stopped accepting new customers on 30 April 2026?
cards.back: **Streaming Video** (live analysis of Kinesis Video Streams feeds) and **Bulk Image Analysis** (batch moderation jobs). Accounts that used them in the last 12 months keep access; image APIs and stored-video jobs are unaffected.
